scope: Four royal-wedding originals viewed at original detail.
globalConditions: Unnamed parable characters; no Jesus likeness or literal portrait of God within the fictional narrative.
Technical source/visual review is not owner approval. Rejected hashes must not be imported.

entries.alt: Two servants stand at a doorway as the older man extends an open hand toward a man standing inside.
entries.caption: The servants bring the king's invitation, but those first invited will not come. The doorway scene pictures an oral summons rather than a written invitation.
entries.findings: Three faces are distinct, with coherent open palm, resting hands and folded arms. Servant's attention reaches the doorway recipient. Photographic stone, fabric and facial detail; no obvious modern or medieval-specific prop.
conditions: Do not claim a named householder, written invitation, exact spoken dialogue or physical violence in this scene.

entries.alt: Two servants in cream tunics and burgundy sashes speak with people beside a road leading toward a palace.
entries.findings: The two principal servants have very similar dark curly hair, beards, face proportions and matching garments; they read as duplicated men rather than clearly distinct messengers. The distant crenellated palace and prominent fleur-de-lis-like royal banners introduce a medieval visual register. Hands and engaged face directions otherwise look coherent.
conditions: Make the servants unmistakably distinct; ideally preserve the older bald gray-bearded servant and younger dark-skinned servant from scene 01.
Replace heraldic banners with plain drapery and simplify the distant building to a plausible ancient palace/courtyard entrance.
The gathered guests should remain mixed; do not label visible people as morally good or bad from appearance.

entries.alt: Guests share food and conversation at crowded banquet tables beneath royal banners.
entries.findings: The central foreground curly-haired bearded man strongly resembles the approved Christ face in brow, nose, smile and beard, despite shorter hair; this invites an unintended Christ identification inside the parable. Repeated gold rampant-lion heraldic banners give the hall a pronounced medieval court appearance. Foreground hands, cups, food contact and social attention are otherwise credible.
conditions: Replace central guest with an unmistakably different fictional face, such as an older balding clean-shaven guest, preserving the gathering action.
Remove heraldic lion banners; use plain textiles and restrained ancient Mediterranean banquet details.
A full hall illustrates Matthew 22:10; do not portray Jesus as a guest or assign unseen biographies.

entries.alt: A king gestures toward a plainly dressed man standing among seated banquet guests.
entries.findings: King and guest have distinct faces and credible reciprocal attention. Open palm, lowered hands and body proportions look coherent. Repeated heraldic lion banners plus heavily ornamented velvet-like green royal clothing give a strong medieval court impression inconsistent with the intended ancient setting.
conditions: Remove heraldic banners and revise royal clothing to simpler layered ancient textiles with restrained trim and a simple diadem; preserve distinct face and questioning action.
Do not explain the missing wedding garment as poverty, inability to afford clothing, or a documented garment-distribution custom; Matthew does not supply those explanations.
The guest's lack of an answer is the source point, not a claim that plain dress determines a person's worth.
